title: The History of King Wird Khan

keywords: the history of king wird khan
full_text:
Upon ascending the throne of Hind, young King Wird Khan at first governed with wisdom under the guidance of the venerable vizier Shimas. However, flattering young courtiers soon whispered poison into the young monarch’s ear: 'Why do you submit your royal will to that ancient graybeard? You are the sovereign! Command whatever your whims desire!'

Intoxicated by pride, Wird Khan dismissed Shimas and the elder counselors, replaced them with reckless favorites, and increased taxes to build extravagant pleasure pavilions.

Within two years, the kingdom was plunged into economic distress: the farmers abandoned their fields, trade ceased, and an army of neighboring invaders massed upon the northern frontier.

Facing sudden ruin, Wird Khan sat alone upon his throne in despair.

Remembering the ancient teachings of Shimas, the young king tore his royal robes, put ashes upon his head, and walked on foot to the humble hermitage where Shimas lived in contemplation.

Wird Khan fell at the sage’s feet, weeping: 'O father of wisdom! I yielded to vanity and brought my kingdom to the brink of the abyss! Forgive my youthful folly and save our people!'

Shimas lifted the weeping king, embraced him with tears of forgiveness, and returned to court. With masterly strategy, Shimas negotiated an honorable peace with the invaders, reorganized the administration, and restored the granaries.

Wird Khan never again yielded to flattering courtiers, ruling for fifty years in humble adherence to wise counsel.
moral: Youthful impatience that casts aside wise counsel brings sudden peril, cured only by humble repentance.
